Subject: ACME POC — next steps & success criteria

Hi Jordan — great call this morning, thanks for the time. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment before drafting the SOW.

Recap of what ACME wants to validate in the PoC:
- Quality: model responses should meet internal accuracy bar for support triage and knowledge-grounded responses (details below).
- Latency: p95 end-to-end latency <= 500ms for typical 512-token prompts.
- Cost: target unit economics under your threshold (approx cost target discussed on call: $X per 1M tokens) — we'll provide a detailed estimate.
- Reliability & safety: hallucination rate < 1% on severity > low; robust FTO for PII handling.

Proposed eval approach (high-level):
1) Offline evals (week 1) — run curated prompt suite (200 prompts across intents) against candidate model variants and rubric.
2) Online shadow (week 2) — 7-day shadow at ~10% sampled traffic to capture end-to-end metrics and user-facing errors.
3) Decision period (week 3) — joint review, cutover plan or follow-up tuning.

Ownership (proposed):
- Redwood: Marissa (sales lead, project coordination), Marcus (SE / infra & shadow routing), Rachel (evals lead / rubric & offline analysis).
- ACME: Jordan (product), Sanjay (engineering lead), procurement will handle standard SOW/PO steps.

Deliverables we will share with you by EOD Wed: POC evaluation plan (scope, prompts, metrics, timeline), evaluation rubric (scoring + pass thresholds), preliminary cost estimate, and a short SOW draft. See attachments: ACME_POC_EvalPlan_v1.xlsx, Redwood_Eval_Rubric_v2.pdf.

Ask: Can you confirm the success criteria above and whether any other metrics matter (e.g., downstream task accuracy, user satisfaction signal)? Also confirm decision makers and procurement timing so we can schedule the SOW draft.

Thanks —

Thanks Jordan — answers inline + more detail and attachments.

1) Offline evals / ground truth:
- We recommend a mixed approach: ACME provides ~100 representative production prompts (anonymized) + Redwood supplies ~100 synthetic/bench prompts covering edge intents. Redwood will run the candidate models against the suite and produce gold labels using our evaluation team. If ACME prefers to own labeling, we can ship a labeling template and support QA.

2) Rubric & weighting (proposed):
- Quality (answer correctness / hallucination): 50% (scored via 1–5 rubric, flagged hallucinations get auto-fail for severity >= medium)
- Latency: 20% (p95 & 99 targets, weighted toward p95)
- Cost: 20% (tokens + infra delta, normalized)
- Reliability/ops (error rate, timeouts): 10%

Pass threshold: aggregate score >= 75% AND no catastrophic hallucination incidents in the shadow window. We include a per-intent breakdown so ACME can require higher thresholds for critical intents. See Redwood_Eval_Rubric_v2.pdf.

3) Online shadow plan:
- 7-day shadow at 10% traffic sampling (mirror requests). Shadow collects end-to-end latencies, top-k responses, and error conditions but does not return to end users. We'll provide dashboards for: latency histograms, 5xx/timeout rate, hallucination flags (auto-detected + sample manual review), and token-cost estimates.

4) Timeline (proposed):
- Week 0 (this week): finalize SOW and PO.
- Week 1: offline eval run + rubric scoring (Rachel leads).
- Week 2: infra prep + 7-day shadow (Marcus leads infra).
- Week 3: joint review + recommendations + optional tuning.

Owners: Marissa (project lead / enablement), Rachel (offline evals + scoring), Marcus (shadow infra, dashboards), Jordan & Sanjay (ACME product & eng leads).

Next steps: I'll attach the sample prompt set and a more detailed evaluation plan. Can you confirm procurement timeline? If procurement can approve by Friday, we can start Week 1 next Monday.

Best —
Marissa
